page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No margin notes. Running head at top, page number at top right. Gathering signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: ad conventum, primùm detrimento id non esset appellanti, deinde præter emansitationis pœnam usitatam, quinque etiam marcas fisco solveret: si latam ab eo sententiam confirmari contingeret, potestatem haberet totam causam porrò definiendi, etiamsi anno suo evoluto magistratu jam abiisset: ad conventum judicialem coeuntibus judicandi gratiâ quantumvis raro numero jus esset ac potestas causas definiendi, non secus ac si frequentes convenissent: Conventus hujusmodi Groningæ agerentur quotannis quater aut sæpius, si Reip. ratio id videretur po-scere: esset-que in eo, ut & in tempore conventuum designando, arbitrium prætorum ab oppidanis datorum (Hovetmannos vocant) & eorum qui res per [?]Agrum in tribunalibus inferioribus judicant: Deinde de fontium pœnis aut mulctis hæc: Furti, latrocinii, proditionis, incendiorum reos receptare fas non esset, aut pœnis eripere: pœna omnium horum, supplicium capitis. Cædes cujusvis hominis in conventu publico præsentis, aut ìstuc euntis, aut redeuntis ab eo, mulctâ lueretur sexcuplâ: idem juris de vulnere, aliâve injuriâ esset: Consulis

page.notes: Printed text runs in mixed roman and italic; italic passages are marked. "per Agrum" has a symbol before "Agrum" that I could not read with confidence. The line "ratio id videretur poscere" is hyphenated as "po-scere" at the line end. The printed "esset-que" is shown with the printed word break "esset-que" kept as one word. The final word "Consulis" ends the page and the catchword "verò" is at the foot. The printed "aut ìstuc" has a stray accent mark over "i", which I have left as printed.
